title: Monitoring memory
subtitle: RAM, swap, and paging — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Snapshot of RAM and swap: total / used / free / cache / available (human-readable)
cards.notes: Answers “how much RAM is left?” Trust available more than free. -h prints M/G sizes.

cards.meaning: Estimate of RAM still usable for new workloads (free + reclaimable cache)
cards.notes: The number to trust. Panic when available is tiny and swap is climbing — not when free alone looks low.

cards.meaning: Kernel buffers + page cache — file data kept in RAM; can be given to apps when needed
cards.notes: Not wasted. Linux loves to fill RAM with cache. Low free + high buff/cache is normal.

cards.meaning: Completely unused RAM (or swap on the Swap row)
cards.example: free column under Mem: in free -h
cards.notes: Do not panic on low free alone — read available. Cache is a spare tank.

cards.meaning: Disk overflow for RAM — total / used / free swap
cards.notes: A little used swap is not always a crisis. Sustained growth with tiny available means RAM pressure.

cards.meaning: Snapshot of procs, memory (active/inactive), swap in/out, I/O, interrupts, CPU
cards.notes: -a shows active/inactive memory instead of the default buffer/cache split. Answers “is it swapping / waiting on I/O right now?”
High r = CPU queue. Pair with idle/us/sy to confirm saturation.
High b = waiting on disk/network I/O, not necessarily needing more CPU.

cards.example: si and so columns in vmstat
cards.notes: Sustained so = RAM pressure (paging out). si/so > 0 and climbing often means thrashing.

cards.example: swpd column under memory in vmstat
cards.notes: Stock of swap in use. Combine with si/so rates to see if paging is active now.

cards.meaning: I/O wait — CPU idle while waiting on block I/O
cards.example: wa in us sy id wa st
cards.notes: Same story as %iowait in mpstat. High wa points to disk, not pure compute need.

cards.meaning: Total number of tasks (forks) created since last boot
cards.notes: Prints a single forks count, not the live table.

cards.meaning: Wide columns; sample every 1 second, 3 times (live)
cards.notes: First line is often since-boot; later lines are the live interval. Same pattern as vmstat 1 3.

cards.meaning: Summary counters dump (total memory, pages swapped, forks, CPU ticks, …)
cards.notes: A dump of totals, not the repeating activity table.
